lenses.first_failed_inequality: None. Every inequality in PROOF sections 2-3, eqs. (2)-(10), re-derives with the stated constants. I attacked the selected-row identity (2), the reduced system (3)-(4), the B_m bound, the S(B_m) bound (6), the cH^2 bound, Phi(B_m)<0 in (7), Phi(b0)>0 in (8), continuity and the IVT, monotonicity of H, the per-coordinate floor, and the dense transfer (9). None of them fails for n>=10^6.

findings.item: (a) Existence, uniqueness, contraction, no periodic orbit
findings.statement: f(h)=tanh(Rh+b0 1) is a contraction with constant ||R||op=a=1-1/n<1 in l2, because tanh is coordinatewise 1-Lipschitz. So h* exists and is unique, and f^p (constant a^p) has no other fixed point, so there is no distinct autonomous periodic orbit. The R0 map is also a contraction, so its fixed point h*_0 is unique.
findings.evidence: Banach fixed-point theorem applied to ||f(h)-f(g)||<=||R(h-g)||<=a||h-g||.

findings.statement: Comparing fixed points gives ||h*-h*_0||<=||R h*-R0 h*_0||<=a||h*-h*_0||+e||h*_0||, so ||h*-h*_0||<=e n||h*_0||<=4/(1e8 sqrt n). This bound holds for every coordinate. At n>=10^6 it is <=4e-11, so m0-4e-11>1/50. For the archived R=(R0+J/(1e8 n^3))a/||.||, ||R-R0||<=|a-||raw|||+n/(1e8 n^3)<=2/(1e8 n^2), half of e_n.
findings.evidence: Analytic derivation. Numerically, the dense-vs-R0 fixed-point shift at n=2000/4000/8000 is 1.7e-13/1.9e-13/1.1e-13, against the bound 1.7e-11/1.4e-11/1.9e-11 computed from the measured ||R-R0||. These shifts are at double-precision noise level because the perturbation is about 1e-15 (fullcheck_out.json).

findings.statement: Re-derived from scratch. w^T w=2(1-tau) gives U=I-cH ww^T. With v_0=0: w^T v=-tau S, Pw=e1-tau 1, w^T Pv=v_(d-1)-tau S, w^T Pw=1-2tau. The coefficient on S in rows i>=1 is tau^2[-2cH+cH^2(1-2tau)]=-cH^2 tau^2. This gives J=cH tau v_(d-1)-cH^2 tau^2 S, with the extra cH tau S only in row 1, exactly as in (2). Oe0=e0 and O^T e0=e0, so the protected coordinate is decoupled in both directions.
findings.evidence: Structured-matvec check against the closed form with random v (v_0=0): max error 1.1e-15/5.6e-16/4.4e-16 at n=2000/4000/8000. Oe0 and O^T e0 errors are <=8.9e-16.

findings.item: (b) Reduced system (3)-(4) is equivalent to the R0 fixed point
findings.statement: Set B=aJ+b0. Then the off-cycle selected rows give v_i=H(B), the cycle bulk gives v_i=tanh(a v_(i-1)+B), and the head gives v_1=tanh(B+a cH tau S). Phi(B)=0 is exactly the statement B=b0+aJ(v(B)). It is equivalent to a cH tau S=(b0-B)/(cH tau)+a v_(d-1), which turns the head equation into the first line of (3). So every root yields an R0 fixed point. Uniqueness of that fixed point makes every root give the same vector; uniqueness of the root is not needed. The cycle map is an a-contraction in sup norm, and v(B), H(B) are continuous in B.
findings.evidence: My own reduced solver (reduced.py) reproduces Codex's archived n=200 and n=2000 minima to about 1e-11 (-0.11760216435, -0.00222571106). It matches brute-force full-R0 iteration to max |diff| 1.7e-15/4.4e-15/2.3e-14 at n=2000/4000/8000, and to 3.6e-12 at n=10^6 (10725 iterations, residual 1e-13).

findings.statement: B_m=(atanh m0-m0)+m0/n<=m0^3/(3(1-m0^2))+m0/10^6=1004797/191880000000~5.24e-6<1e-5. Since 0<B_m<b0, the extra forcing is positive. The cycle stays in [m0,1], and the mean value theorem with tanh'<=1-m0^2 gives a cycle excess <=(1-m0)/m0^2=1560 (the proof states 1600). The dropped term -a cH tau v_(d-1) is negative. k>=500000 gives tau<1/700 and cH^2<1.00287<201/200. The exact upper bound for Phi(B_m) is -21649/1e6. In (8), cH tau^2 r=(1-tau^2)/(1-tau)=1+tau, so Phi(b0)=a cH H(b0)>0. H'(B)=(1-H^2)/(1-a(1-H^2))>0, so B*>B_m implies H(B*)>m0. Protected and source coordinates exceed tanh(b0)=0.04996>m0.
findings.evidence: Exact rationals in checks2.py. Numerically at n=10^6: Phi(B_m)=-0.02482 (bound -0.021649), cycle excess at B_m=69.8 (bound 1560), and Phi(b0)=0.502779=a cH H(b0) exactly.

findings.statement: Each coordinate class is covered. Protected: z=tanh(az+b0)~0.502. Cycle head: about 1. Cycle bulk and tail: >=H(B*). Off-cycle: =H(B*). Source: >tanh(b0). All exceed m0=1/40 on R0, and are >=1/50 on the dense R after (9). The chain only uses k>=500000, so it holds uniformly for n>=10^6. The proof needs Theorem 1 only through |h*_i|>=m, which Lemma 2 and (17) require, and that is supplied.
findings.evidence: Analytic. The minimizing coordinate is always the off-cycle bulk H(B*) (brute-force argmin index = d at n=2000/4000/8000).

findings.item: (c) Numerical h*_0 structure at large n
findings.statement: Min h*_0 by n (the minimizer is always the off-cycle bulk H(B*), which equals the decayed cycle tail at large n): 1e4: 0.041084099; 3e4: 0.047166496; 1e5: 0.049049379; 1e6: 0.049820545; 1e7: 0.049929375; 1e8: 0.049950657. Other levels: protected about 0.50192 to 0.50207, cycle head 0.99827 at 1e4 and 1-O(e^-70) at large n, source 0.0499584 (just above tanh(b0)). Asymptotically H=tanh(b0-a cH tau H-a cH^2 Ex/k), where the cycle excess Ex->33.6. So h_off = tanh(b0) - sech^2(b0)[tanh(b0)sqrt(2/n)+67/n] + ..., which tends to tanh(0.05)=0.049958375.
findings.evidence: reduced_large.json. The self-consistent formula matches H to 1.6e-15 at n=1e6 and 1e8. The brute-force full-R0 iteration at n=1e6 gives min 0.049820545369907, agreeing with the reduced solver.

findings.statement: min h*_0 is <=0 up to n=2105 (-2.3e-5) and >0 from n=2106 (+6.4e-5) onward. It is <=1/50 up to n=3553 (0.0199949) and >1/50 from n=3554 (0.0200239). The dependence on n has a sawtooth from floor(n/2), floor(n/4): 1045 small downward steps of size <=3.7e-6 in the 2000-4000 scan. Conclusion (5) is false at practical widths n<=3553, and some coordinates are negative for n<=2105. This is outside the stated scope n>=10^6, and CHECKS.md discloses the n=200/2000 negative minima.
findings.evidence: Every integer n in 2000..4000 was scanned (scan_2000_4000.json). A 244-width log-spaced scan over [3554, 10^6+3], covering all four residues of n mod 4, has worst min 0.020023 at n=3555, so it stays >1/50.

findings.item: (d) Gate gap and near-criticality at moderate width
findings.statement: Because O is orthogonal, ||G* R0||op = a(1-min_i h*_i^2) exactly; the numerical match to 1e-15 confirms it. The gap min h*^2 is 4.95e-6 at n=2000, about 4e-9 at n~2106, 5.6e-4 at 4000, 1.48e-3 at 8000, 2.48e-3 at 1e6, with limit tanh^2(b0)=2.496e-3. Near n~2000-2200, about n/4 off-cycle coordinates have |h*|<0.003. There ||G*R||~a=1-1/n, so the autonomous endpoint is near-critical, Lemma 2's effective kappa tends to 1, and the transport budget H_R would become n-scale. The Theorem 4 mechanism therefore gives nothing there. This lies outside the theorem's scope (n>=10^6, where the gap is about 2.5e-3, versus m^2=4e-4 used in the proof). The theorem's own bound is in any case only nontrivial near n~10^80 for R_abs=1.

findings.item: Sharpening: reach of the same IVT argument
findings.statement: With m0=1/40, the same analytic chain, using exact cH and the 1560 excess, already closes for n>=~126836 rather than 10^6. At n=10^6 it proves h*_0>=0.049028 (largest admissible m0), against the stated m0=1/40. That would allow m~0.049 and kappa~1/(1+6e-4) instead of 10000/10001. The constants are valid but loose, and nothing downstream needs this.
findings.evidence: sharpen.py: U(n,m0)<0 from n~126836; largest provable m0 is 0.0490283 (1e6), 0.0498375 (1e7), 0.0499367 (1e8). The numerically true threshold for (5) is n=3554.

findings.evidence: arithmetic.py lines ~143-152.

lenses.strongest_counterexample_attempt: I re-derived (2) independently, built a reduced-system solver from scratch, and validated it against brute-force full-R0 iteration at n=2000/4000/8000 and n=10^6 (agreement to <=3.6e-12). I then searched for small or negative coordinates of h* at n>=10^6 (1e6/1e7/1e8, min 0.04982 to 0.04995), probed floor-parity effects in a 244-width parity/log scan up to 1e6, and tested whether the dropped term, the S bound (actual excess 69.8 vs bound 1560), the cH^2 bound or the dense perturbation could reverse the sign of Phi(B_m). Nothing failed. The only failures are at practical widths outside scope: negative coordinates for n<=2105, coordinates below 1/50 for n<=3553, and a near-critical endpoint (||G*R||~1-1/n) around n~2100.
lenses.sharpest_correct_statement: For every n>=10^6 (and in fact, by the same analytic chain, every n>=~1.27e5), the unique autonomous fixed point of the actual dense R satisfies h*_i>=1/40-4/(1e8 sqrt n)>1/50 in every coordinate. At n=10^6 the same argument certifies h*_i>=0.04903. The minimizing coordinate is the off-cycle selected bulk H(B*)=tanh(b0)-sech^2(b0)[tanh(b0)sqrt(2/n)+~67/n]+..., which tends to tanh(0.05)=0.0499584. Consequently ||G*R||op=a(1-min h*^2)<=a(1-1/2500). Numerically, (5) already holds from n=3554 on. Below n=2106 some coordinates are negative, and near n~2100 the endpoint is near-critical with gap ~1/n. That regime is outside the theorem's scope and is disclosed in CHECKS.md.

lenses.first_failed_inequality: None. I re-derived Lemma 2 (16), the radial bound (17), (18)-(22) and (36)-(37) from the model and every one holds with the stated constants. The looseness is real but never invalidates a claim. The large constants enter at (22) (q_g=1-1e-4, while the true gate at h* is 1-H^2 ~ 1-2.5e-3) and at the step (36)->(37), which uses ||xi||<=a/beta, i.e. assumes perfect query-sensitivity alignment that the frozen head/rotation cannot deliver.

findings.statement: For all p,z in (-1,1): (atanh z - atanh p)/(z-p) = int_0^1 1/(1-y_s^2) ds >= int_0^1 (1+y_s^2) ds = 1+(p^2+pz+z^2)/3 >= 1+p^2/4, where y_s=p+s(z-p). The last step holds because min_z (p^2+pz+z^2) = 3p^2/4, attained at z=-p/2. So the lemma actually holds for every p in (-1,1). The hypothesis |p|>=m only makes the constant uniform. The bound is nearly tight at z=-p/2: the slack is 2.2e-8 at p=0.02.
findings.evidence: A grid with p in ±[0.02,0.999999] (8002 values) and z in (-1+1e-9,1-1e-9) (20003 values, including +-1e-12 and 0) gives min secant/(1+p^2/4) = 1.000000022 at p=0.02, z=-0.01. At 50 digits, p=0.02 and z=-p/2 give secant 1.000100022006 against 1.0001. Script: wf3_contraction/e1_lemma2.py; output in e1_out.txt.

findings.item: Radial bound (17): domain and what it contracts
findings.statement: Since h*=tanh(Rh*+b) exactly, atanh(h_t)-atanh(h*) = R(h_{t-1}-h*)+x_t =: v_t, coordinate by coordinate, with no approximation. Lemma 2 with p=h*_i>=m (THEOREM 1, all coordinates including protected and source) gives |u_{t,i}|<=kappa|v_{t,i}|, so ||u_t||<=kappa||v_t||<=kappa(a||u_{t-1}||+||x_t||). This holds for ANY h_{t-1} in (-1,1)^n (negative, near 0, near +-1), before burn-in, after arbitrary inputs, and with the dense R (only ||R||=a is used). It contracts ONLY the distance to the single point h*. It does NOT contract differences between two non-fixed trajectories: two nearby states both near 0 separate at the incremental factor of up to a=1-1/n. It also does NOT contract sensitivities; those are controlled only through the good/bad gate classification. The paper states this distinction correctly.
findings.evidence: At n=1e6 with the actual dense R and actual h*, I tested wild previous states: uniform(-1,1), within 1e-6 of +1 and of -1, N(0,1e-4), -h*, -h*/2, h*+1e-9 noise. Inputs were x=0, N(0,1e-3), N(0,10), and an exact landing at -h*/2. The worst ratio ||h_t-h*||/(kappa||v_t||) is 0.9976 (attained near h*), and every ratio is <=1. Script: e3_radial.py; output in e3_out.txt.

findings.statement: Unrolling y_t<=kappa a y_{t-1}+kappa||x_t|| (nonnegative comparison) gives y_t <= (kappa a)^t sqrt(n) + sum_s kappa(kappa a)^{t-s}||x_s||. Over t>=L_n, the initial term has time-l2 norm <= (m/2)/sqrt(1-kappa^2) = 0.01*10001/sqrt(20001) = 0.7071. Young's inequality (an l1 kernel convolved with l2 inputs) bounds the convolution by ||k||_1 R = [kappa/(1-kappa)] R = 1e4 R. Only the l2 input energy is used; no l1 norm of the inputs appears. Two related steps are also correct: the pointwise bound (23) uses the kernel's l2 norm, 10000/sqrt(20001) = 70.71 < 71, and the pre-burn-in bound R sqrt(t) is Cauchy-Schwarz over a finite window. L_n=ceil(log(100 sqrt n)/log(1.0001)) matches arithmetic.py and gives kappa^{L_n} sqrt(n) <= m/2.
findings.evidence: This is a direct derivation; the constants are exact rationals. Numerical runs (n=1e5, started from h_0=0, burn-in counted): tiny forcing with R=0.005 gives sum_{t>=L} ||u||^2 = 2.02, far below the bound 2601. R=0.02 gives 32.3 against 4.04e4. A single pulse with R=0.2 gives 11.07 against 4.0e6. Script: e7_forcing.py; output in e7_out.txt.

findings.item: Bad-step count (21) plus a rigorous sharpening (an energy-to-gate-defect inequality)
findings.statement: (21) holds: #bad*(m/2)^2 < sum||u_t||^2 <= (0.7071+1e4R)^2, so #bad < 1e4(1+1e4R)^2 <= B_R. The same argument gives more. Define the number of COORDINATE-steps N_delta = #{(t,i): t>=L_n, |h_{t,i}|<=delta}. For delta<m, each such pair has |u_{t,i}| >= h*_i-delta >= m-delta, so N_delta <= (0.7071+1e4R)^2/(m-delta)^2. In particular, keeping s coordinates at |h|<=delta for tau steps after burn-in requires R >= ((m-delta)sqrt(s tau)-0.7071)/1e4. A construction realises R ~ B* sqrt(s tau) with B*=4.13e-5, so the sqrt(s tau) law is sharp up to a factor of about 20.
findings.evidence: Derivation above. For the construction, holding one coordinate at exactly 0 costs |atanh(H)-aH| = B* = 4.163e-5 per step (n->inf limit; 4.133e-5 measured at n=1e6). Holding it at deviation just above m/2 costs 2.05e-5 per step. So the true maximum is about 2.4e9 bad steps per unit energy, against the paper's 1e12. The R^2 exponent is sharp; the constant is about 420x loose.

findings.item: Good-step gate bound, product bound and transport sum (22)
findings.statement: Good step: ||u_t||_2<=m/2 implies ||u_t||_inf<=m/2 implies h_{t,i}>=h*_i-m/2>=m/2, so the gate is <=1-m^2/4=q_g and ||G_tR||<=q_g a. Bad step: ||G_tR||<=a<1. A length-j window after L_n contains at most B_R bad steps, which gives the product bound <= q_g^{max(0,j-B_R)}. The sum is (B_R+1)+q_g/(1-q_g) = B_R+10000 = H_R exactly. No q_g^{-B_R} prefactor arises.
findings.evidence: Direct derivation. At n=1e5 the true gate at good steps is <=0.99760 (the max gate observed under tiny forcing), compared with q_g=0.9999. So the good-step rate is conservative by a factor of about 25 (H^2 = 2.5e-3 versus m^2/4 = 1e-4).

findings.item: Sensitivity bound (36) and THEOREM 4 (37): uniform over arbitrary T
findings.statement: The injection satisfies ||E K h_{t-1,src}|| <= ||K||_F ||h_src|| <= sqrt(l) because |tanh|<1, and h_0=0 makes the first injection zero. With gates <=1 and ||R||=a, ||B_t||<=sqrt(l)t for t<=L_n. For T>L_n, unrolling (1) gives B_T = Pi A B_{L_n} + sum_s (Pi_{t=s+1}^T A_t) G_s inj_s, so ||B_T|| <= sqrt(l)L_n + sqrt(l) sum_j q_g^{max(0,j-B_R)} = sqrt(l)(L_n+H_R). B_R is independent of T, so the bound is uniform over all horizons. (37) then follows from (12)-(13): w_R/beta=1/n and ||A_j||<=a for every legal future gate. The onset (38) and the necessary-energy bound (39) follow arithmetically: L_n<=10002 log n, and at n=1e80, R=1, eps=1e-3, (4H_R/eps)^2 ~ 1.6e31 < 1e80.
findings.evidence: Direct derivation. All measured ||B_T K|| (forward mode, actual model) are far below sqrt(l)(L_n+H_R). Examples: 2.06e5 against 1.09e12 at n=1e5, and 1.42e4 against 3.54e12 at n=1e6.

findings.statement: This attack is covered. The time-l2 bound needs only l2 energy; the l1 norm R sqrt(T), which is unbounded, never enters. Tiny forcing can produce many steps that are 'bad' by the norm test, but the steady deviation per step is about R/(H^2 sqrt T), so no gate opens. These steps are bad by norm only and are harmless for transport, so the bound over-charges them.
findings.evidence: At n=1e5, R=0.005 over 20000 steps gives 18408 norm-bad steps (B_R=2.6e7), but the maximum gate stays at 0.997599 < q_g. R=0.02 gives 19886 bad steps with maximum gate 0.997613.

findings.item: Attack: single or sparse pulses; how long one O(1)-energy pulse keeps a coordinate near critical
findings.statement: Off-cycle coordinates recover by x -> tanh(a x + B*) with B* = atanh(H)-aH ~ H^3/3 ~ 4.1e-5, and cycle-plateau holes behave the same way in the co-moving frame. Recovery from 0 therefore takes O(H/B*) = O(1/H^2) steps, independent of n. One pulse of any size keeps one coordinate bad (|u|>0.01) for at most about 2590 steps and near-critical (|h|<0.01) for at most about 480 steps. Size beyond about 0.2 does not help, because tanh saturates and recovery from -1 is fast. Spreading the energy over N pulses gives about N*O(1/H^2) bad steps, which is always inside B_R. A late pulse before T is likewise covered: the decoder stores h_T, and a common-endpoint pair must pay for a landing.
findings.evidence: Scalar runs at the measured B*,H for n=1e4, 1e5, 1e6 and n->inf: a creation pulse of energy 0.0025 gives 1135-1381 bad steps and 235-375 near-critical steps, converging as n grows (e4_out.txt). Pulse amplitudes 0.2, 0.5, 1, 3 give 2526, 2584, 2589, 2590 bad steps. Full-model pulses at n=1e5: N=1 (R=0.2) gives 1104 bad steps; N=20 gives 12797 (e7_out.txt).

findings.item: Attack: holes that co-move with the cycle P at zero input cost; dense or Householder spreading
findings.statement: Co-moving holes are not free. A moving zero-hole drifts upward by B* per step, so maintenance costs B*^2 = 1.7e-9 per step, independent of n. Left unmaintained, it recovers in about 1135 bad steps. The cycle is also not a closed loop. Because O = U P U, the uniform selected mode maps onto e_1, giving h*_1 ~ 1 with preactivation ~ sqrt(k)H ~ 35 and a head region of about 1435 elevated coordinates at n=1e6. Every hole and any sensitivity carried around the cycle is erased at the head, so one pass lasts at most d minus about 1435 steps. The radial bound is a norm bound, so rotation or spreading cannot evade it. The 1e8 n^3 dense part and the O(tau) Householder coupling enter only through ||R||=a.
findings.evidence: Actual h* at n=1e6: min 0.049821 (>=1/50, consistent with THEOREM 1); cycle head 1.0, 0.7616, 0.6420, ...; plateau H=0.0498205; B*=4.133e-5. Results in e2_out_1e6.txt. In the full-model held-hole runs, every hole step is bad (bad=tau) and the hole costs about 0.005 in total (creation plus landing) plus tau*1.7e-9.

findings.item: Attack: coordinate concentration (1, sqrt n, n^alpha coordinates)
findings.statement: Holding s coordinates costs s times as much per step but does not increase the number of bad TIME steps. For the operator norm: with K spread over s off-cycle holes, ||B_T K|| ~ sigma* sqrt(l) tau, independent of s. For the visible credit: the future query can concentrate on only one cycle coordinate, and the patterned part sees at most ~0.17/sqrt(n) per coordinate. So at fixed energy, s=1 is optimal and sqrt(n)- or n^alpha-coordinate holes are strictly worse. All such schedules are inside B_R and also inside the coordinate-step bound N_delta.
findings.evidence: Derivation, plus the off-cycle and cycle numerics below.

findings.item: Is H_R ~ 1e12 R^2 sharp in exponent?
findings.statement: Yes for (36). One off-cycle coordinate (a self-loop of weight a) held at 0 for tau steps, at cost about 2H^2 + tau B*^2, gives ||B_T K|| ~ 0.9 sigma* sqrt(l) tau with sigma*=tanh(.05), for K=e_i c^T, while tau <~ n. So ||B_T||op >~ 0.05 sqrt(l) (R^2-2H^2)/B*^2 ~ 2.9e7 sqrt(l) R^2, until it saturates at R ~ B* sqrt(n). Both the R^2 exponent and the sqrt(l) factor of (36) are therefore attained. The constant 1e12 is loose by about 3.4e4.
findings.evidence: At n=1e5 (off-cycle, forward-mode s_T), ||s_T|| = 26578 at tau=2000 and 205678 at tau=20000: linear in tau. The baseline is 4613. Files: e5_offcycle_n100000_tau*.json.

findings.item: True scaling of the VISIBLE normalized credit (the Theorem-4 quantity) with R and n
findings.statement: The large looseness sits in (36)->(37). The legal L=1 query with q uniform gives beta*xi = R^T G_f q ~ 0.665 e_{d-1}: O(1) visibility on one cycle coordinate. The coherent off-cycle sensitivity is seen only at weight O(1/sqrt n) or less (the uniform query gives about 1/k). Cycle-hole sensitivity is visible but accumulates only incoherently. Heuristic fit for one maintained co-moving hole: credit ~ 0.0235 sqrt(tau/n), with tau ~ R^2/B*^2 and tau <= d minus the head, i.e. ~ 570 R/sqrt(n). The n-exponent n^{-1/2} of delta_0 is right: even the zero-input public baseline credit is ~0.33/sqrt(n). The R-dependence of the true visible credit appears to be ~R rather than R^2, and the constant is loose by about 1e9 or more. Consequence (HEURISTIC): an eps=1e-3 robust pair (difference >2eps) needs only R ~ sqrt(0.005+1.26e-11 n). For R=1, robust pairs should persist up to n ~ 8e10, compared with the proven no-section onset of 1e80. The necessary-energy exponent 1/4 in (39) is valid but likely not sharp; the heuristic exponent is 1/2. None of this contradicts THEOREM 4.
findings.evidence: Full actual-model runs from h_0=0 count every input (prefix landing, hole creation, maintenance, exact landing). Both branches end EXACTLY at h* (residual <1e-11) at the same time; the query is L=1 with all future preactivations 1/4 and K uniform over the visited rows. Credit difference at n=1e5, R~0.0694: 6.9e-4 (tau=500), 2.51e-3 (2000), 5.07e-3 (8000), 5.55e-3 (20000; saturation from the tau/n and tau/k leak). At n=1e6, inside the theorem's range, R=0.0705: 8.35e-4 (tau=2000). At n=1e6, R=0.0706: 2.41e-3 (tau=12000), i.e. half-distance 1.2e-3 > eps. The theorem's delta_0 bound at these R is 3.5e6, so it is vacuous there but consistent. Files: SUMMARY_holes.json, e5*_cycle_*.json.

findings.statement: The hole constructions give LOWER-side evidence for specific K, specific legal queries and specific pairs. They are numerics at n=1e5 and 1e6 plus scaling heuristics, not all-n theorems. I do not establish that they form a positive-dimensional antipodal section in the accepted sense. They show only that the theorem's onset and its n^{1/4} necessary-energy exponent are far from sharp. The theorem itself already labels these as conservative.

I pushed one coordinate to 0 and kept the hole open, either co-moving along the cycle P (moving input -B* per step) or parked on an off-cycle self-loop (row weight a=1-1/n). Each hole step is a bad step, so the attack consumes the bad-step budget as efficiently as is possible here, at about 1.7e-9 energy per step. The off-cycle hole makes ||B_T K|| grow linearly (2.06e5 at tau=20000, n=1e5), which matches the R^2*sqrt(l) form of (36). The cycle hole gives the largest visible credit difference for a legal L=1 query: 2.41e-3 at n=1e6 and R=0.0706. Both stay far inside sqrt(l)(L_n+H_R) and delta_0 (3.5e6 at that R), because B_R ~ 5e9 >> tau. The attack fails to refute the theorem for a structural reason: bad steps are counted from the l2-in-time state energy, which the radial bound controls globally. Neither tiny long forcing, pulses, co-moving holes, Householder/dense spreading nor coordinate concentration can create bad steps beyond about 2.4e9 R^2, and the paper allows 1e12 R^2.

findings.statement: The decomposition is exact. Hold all realized raw inputs fixed and write F_j dtheta = dR h_(j-1) + dW x_j + db and Phi(t,s) = A_t...A_(s+1) with A_j = G_j R. Then grad of q^T h_(T+L)/beta equals S_T^* xi_Q plus the sum over j=T+1..T+L of F_j^* G_j Phi(T+L,j)^T q/beta, where xi_Q = Phi(T+L,T)^T q/beta. For j>T we have h_j = tanh(v_j), G_j = sech^2(v_j) and x_j = v_j - R h_(j-1) - b. So xi_Q depends only on (R, v), and the direct part depends only on (R, W, b, h_T, v); h_T enters only through h_T in the R injection and x_(T+1) in the W injection. The same holds for the selected block: past = B_T^* xi_Q restricted to rows 1..k-1 and source columns.

findings.item: (b) eq. (13): uniform query bound and amplification
findings.statement: The bound holds: sup_Q w_R ||DeltaB^* xi_Q||_F <= w_R ||DeltaB||op (a^L/beta) <= (a/n)||DeltaB||op, using ||A_j|| <= ||G_j|| ||R|| <= a. It is an upper bound, never an equality, and the text does not claim equality. No query alignment can exceed the operator norm. The structure O^T 1_k = sqrt(k)(e_(d-1) + gamma tau e0 - gamma tau^2 1_k) concentrates what uniform-gate queries see, but this cannot raise the upper bound. findings.item: (b) metric: nu_n versus the Frobenius group norm
findings.statement: The accepted nu_n (codex_intermediate_gate_credit_20261002/PROOF.md:46-50; query_visible_operator_dimension_20261002/PROOF.md:96-107) is the normalized gradient's Frobenius norm restricted to K = p H^T/||H|| with a fixed source H = .4*1_l. The new theorem bounds the Frobenius norm of the whole selected r x l block with time-varying true sources. That dominates every fixed-direction restriction K = p u^T, so 'bounds every one-fixed-feature restriction in unchanged units' is correct. Scope note: the accepted fixed-source-H lower families are not in the constant-absolute-energy class at large n. Each step that sets or holds the source at .4 costs raw input of about (atanh(.4) - .05) sqrt(l) ~ 0.374 sqrt(l). The theorem therefore governs a class disjoint from those lower families, as the authors intend (REPORT section 1), and contradicts none of them.

findings.item: (c) zero-credit encoder versus the accepted continuous no-replay contract
findings.statement: The encoder E_t = h_t, U(E,x) = tanh(RE + x + b) is continuous, causal and uses public weights, with no tape, replay or clock. The decoder is the exact direct part, which is smooth in h_T for fixed Q. This matches the accepted counting rules, and '0 credit coordinates' is meaningful under them: the stored h is used only to compute the exact direct terms, and at a public common endpoint even h is public. Quoted rules: query_weighted_moment_merger_20261001/PROOF.md:47-50 ('All actual future injections are included exactly. The encoder approximates only the past term Z^T c_q. Storing true current h costs n coordinates; if h is supplied, omit those n ... No discarded-history replay or tape'); codex_online_gate_polynomial_20261002/PROOF.md:105-109 ('plus n current hidden-state coordinates while processing actual inputs. Public time, ... model weights are uncounted ... Arithmetic workspace and final output storage are not persistent'); codex_causal_suffix_width_20261002/PROOF.md:383-395 ('Forward h costs another n if raw inputs rather than D are supplied').

Bound. For every query (any L >= 1 and any future gates in (0,1], so in particular every accepted [1/4,3/4]^n preactivation query, with inputs held fixed and q, beta, w_R frozen), the normalized past contribution of the selected block satisfies
w_R ||B_T^* xi_Q||_F <= (a^L/n)||B_T||op <= a sqrt(l)(L_n + H_R)/n <= (L_n + H_R)/sqrt n.

This holds for every R_abs >= about 0.006 (ramped) or 0.071 (abrupt), so R in {1,4,16} give identical maxima, because T_R=R^2/B*^2 >= 5.8e8 is much larger than n. Decay begins only once n exceeds about 5.8e8 R^2. The extrapolated sup credit falls below eps/2=5e-4 for log10 n > 21.2 (R=1), 23.6 (R=4), 26.0 (R=16), 16.6 (R=0.0711). The theorem's own delta_0 < eps/2 holds for log10 n > 30.3 / 32.7 / 35.1, so the stated 10^80 onset is valid. delta_0 beats the trivial ceiling a*sqrt(l) only for n > 1e12 R^2. The theorem is nonvacuous only astronomically, as REPORT disclaims.
findings.evidence: extrapolate.py and extrapolate2.py (mpmath, 130 digits, actual B*(n), H(n), sigma(n)). The ramp fixed cost E0 is about 3e-5, as measured in the full model and the scalar optimum. findings.item: (b) Holding cost (35) and the no-periodic-orbit claim

findings.item: (c) Consistency with the accepted Omega(n^(19/18)), Omega(n^(16/15)) and zero-endpoint results
findings.statement: The accepted lower-bound sections satisfy every hypothesis of Theorem 4 except the constant energy budget: same frozen R, h_0=0, n>=10^900>=10^6, same legal one-step query, inputs in the cube, and no endpoint or gate hypothesis needed.
